article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Undisclosed proprietary parent genetics
Breeder: Dutch Passion
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Pine, lemon, sweet fruit, spice, Skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–12 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 500–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Few marijuana strains earn a name as ambitious as The Ultimate and then build their reputation primarily on measurable garden performance. Dutch Passion introduced this balanced hybrid to combine unusually heavy flower production with the resin, potency, and smoking quality expected from premium cannabis. Instead of advertising an elaborate genetic pedigree, the breeder has deliberately kept the parents secret, allowing the finished cultivar to stand on its own merits. What is known is that the plant behaves much like an exceptionally productive old-school Skunk : vigorous without being unmanageable, heavily resinous, pungent, and capable of producing enormous elongated flowers during the final weeks of bloom. Dutch Passion classifies it as a 50/50 indica-sativa hybrid and currently lists a 9–12-week flowering period with an XXL yield rating.
Genetics and Lineage

The exact lineage of The Ultimate remains proprietary. Dutch Passion explicitly states that the original parents have never been disclosed because the breeder wanted the cultivar recognized as a distinct variety rather than marketed through the reputation of its ancestors. What the company does reveal is that the genetics produce characteristics comparable to a powerful, easy-growing Skunk, including enormous yields, strong potency, robust growth, and flowers that occasionally display a more sativa-like appearance while becoming much thicker than typical narrow-leaf buds.

That secrecy is important when discussing this strain accurately. Various secondary sources have attempted to attach specific parents to The Ultimate, but none of those proposed pedigrees should replace the breeder’s own documentation. The defensible genetic description is therefore an undisclosed 50/50 indica-sativa hybrid developed and stabilized by Dutch Passion. The company says the variety originated after extensive breeding and the discovery of an exceptional phenotype that combined production, resin, aroma, potency, and overall flower quality.

The result carries unmistakable traits from older European cannabis breeding. Dark green foliage contrasts with lighter flowers covered in orange pistils and abundant trichomes, while the aroma combines Skunk-like pungency with pine, fruit, earth, and fuel. Its branches can produce flowers of unusual length and thickness, making plant structure and production every bit as important to the cultivar’s identity as its psychoactive profile.
Effects and Experience

The Ultimate does not fit neatly into the conventional distinction between an energetic sativa and a sedating indica. Its 50/50 genetic balance becomes apparent shortly after consumption. The onset can be relatively quick, producing an obvious cerebral shift accompanied by elevated mood and a growing sense of physical ease. Dutch Passion characterizes the high as powerful and long-lasting and specifically warns that its intensity can continue building after the first inhalations.

Mental effects can include increased creativity, engagement with music, easier conversation, and a comfortable uplift. Underneath that brighter opening, the indica side gradually develops into deeper bodily relaxation. At modest amounts, the strain can remain surprisingly functional; increase the dose and the experience becomes much heavier. Earlier Dutch Passion grow reports describe it as capable of catching even experienced cannabis consumers off guard because the strength continues accumulating rather than revealing itself all at once.

That progression makes dosage especially important. Someone seeking a balanced recreational experience may prefer a smaller serving that preserves the uplifting portion of the high. Greater consumption can turn the same weed into a powerful evening cultivar with pronounced physical heaviness and reduced motivation. Current breeder materials categorize potency as “very high,” while earlier Dutch Passion information places typical THC around 15–20% and reports that optimized examples can exceed 20%.
Medical Benefits

The combination of cerebral uplift and progressively stronger physical relaxation explains why The Ultimate has attracted some medical marijuana consumers. A balanced hybrid can be appealing when someone wants a noticeable change in mood without immediately becoming inactive, while the heavier later stage may be useful to consumers seeking a more physically calming experience.

Dutch Passion has historically associated the strain with relaxation and relief from discomfort, but those breeder observations should not be interpreted as clinical proof. The Ultimate itself has not been established in controlled trials as a treatment for chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical disorder. Named cannabis cultivars can also vary chemically from one harvest to another.

Its potency deserves particular consideration for medical use. Strong THC-dominant weed can produce unwanted anxiety, dizziness, cognitive impairment, or rapid heart rate in sensitive individuals. A laboratory analysis of the actual flower provides better information for medical decision-making than a generalized strain description.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma becomes increasingly difficult to ignore as flowering progresses. Dutch Passion describes mature plants as pungent, with pine, petrol, citrus, spice, and occasional sweeter fruit tones developing late in bloom. Once dried, the flowers can initially smell earthy and spicy; grinding them releases more fruit and pine, revealing a broader aromatic range underneath the stronger Skunk foundation.

Flavor follows a similar sequence. Pine and lemon provide a bright opening, followed by sweet fruit and warm spice before earth and gasoline-like pungency arrive on the finish. Some phenotypes lean noticeably sweeter, while others emphasize traditional Skunk and fuel. This variation prevents The Ultimate from feeling like a modern single-note fruit strain. Its flavor is closer to classic Dutch marijuana, where sweet resin, citrus, pine, spice, and cannabis funk overlap rather than being selected around one dessert aroma.

Dutch Passion does not publish a standardized laboratory terpene profile for the cultivar. Pine suggests that pinene-family aromas may contribute, and citrus frequently accompanies limonene-rich cannabis, but aroma alone cannot establish terpene concentration. Individual laboratory testing is necessary to identify the dominant compounds in a specific crop.
Growing Information

Production is where The Ultimate separates itself from most hybrids. Dutch Passion currently describes indoor yields of approximately 500–600 g/m² as readily achievable, while Screen of Green gardens can exceed 600 g/m². Highly optimized environments have produced more than 750 g/m². Independent breeder grow reports also demonstrate why those figures are believable: one documented crop produced 1,650 grams from 15 plants, averaging approximately 114 grams per plant.

Plants usually finish around 75 cm to 1 meter indoors, although individual specimens can grow taller. The first several weeks after the switch to 12/12 lighting produce moderate-to-high stretch in both height and width. Once that phase ends, flower development accelerates dramatically. During the final three or four weeks, previously ordinary-looking buds can swell into extremely long, dense colas, and branches may bend beneath their weight. Dutch Passion recommends using a net, ties, or other support before this late bulking phase becomes extreme.

The cultivar handles soil, coco, and hydroponic systems and responds particularly well to SCROG cultivation. Strong flowering light helps maximize production, while humidity should remain below roughly 50% during bloom because unusually thick flowers create conditions where mold can become a concern. Outdoors, the plant can become very large and potentially carry several kilograms of flower, but Dutch Passion recommends warm, dry climates or controlled greenhouses rather than cool, damp regions. The breeder specifically advises patience: harvesting too early sacrifices the extraordinary late-stage swelling for which this weed is famous.
FAQ
Is The Ultimate strain indica or sativa?

The Ultimate is an evenly balanced hybrid containing approximately 50% indica and 50% sativa genetics. Dutch Passion selected it to combine the physical depth and flower density associated with indica cannabis with more cerebral qualities and sativa-influenced bud structure.
What are the genetics of The Ultimate?

Dutch Passion has never disclosed the original parental strains. The breeder intentionally keeps the pedigree secret and describes the cultivar as a stable hybrid with traits reminiscent of a powerful, extremely high-yielding old-school Skunk.
How much THC does The Ultimate have?

Dutch Passion classifies the strain as very high in THC. Historical breeder specifications commonly place it around 15–20%, while optimized examples have been reported above 20%. Actual concentration depends on phenotype, environment, lighting, harvest timing, and laboratory methodology.
What does The Ultimate taste like?

The flavor combines pine, lemon and citrus, sweet fruit, spice, earth, Skunk, and gasoline. Dried flowers can initially appear earthy and spicy before grinding releases brighter fruit and pine aromas.
How long does The Ultimate take to flower?

Dutch Passion currently gives a flowering period of approximately 9–12 weeks. Considerable flower weight develops during the final two to four weeks, making patience especially important with this cultivar.
Final Thoughts on The Ultimate

The Ultimate earned its reputation by solving a difficult breeding problem: producing unusually large quantities of marijuana without reducing the finished flower to an ordinary commercial crop. Dutch Passion’s undisclosed 50/50 genetics create a medium-sized plant capable of filling its branches with enormous resinous flowers while still delivering substantial potency, complex flavor, and a long-lasting hybrid experience.

Its biggest advantage is obvious in the garden. Yields around 500–600 g/m² are realistic breeder figures rather than exceptional one-off claims, and skilled growers can push production considerably higher. Yet quantity is only part of the appeal. Pine, lemon, fruit, spice, earth, fuel, and old-school Skunk aromas give the flowers personality, while the effect moves from cerebral uplift toward increasingly powerful physical relaxation. For growers willing to support the heavy branches and allow the full 9–12-week bloom to finish, The Ultimate remains one of Dutch Passion’s clearest examples of cannabis bred around both quality and exceptional production.
